bull_bear.body:
- Established legacy and trusted brand - more than six decades of industry experience in thermal management and sealing solutions, with a reputation for quality and reliability among OEMs, replacement-market partners and global customers
- Diversified customer, product and geographic base across automotive, agriculture, construction, industrial, power generation and aftermarket segments, reducing overdependence on any single customer, sector or geography
- Strong in-house engineering and R&D - design, testing, validation and product development capabilities enabling customised solutions aligned with changing emission norms (BS-VI, BS-IV/Trem V, CPCB IV+)
- Long-standing relationships with leading domestic and global OEMs, providing visibility into technology trends and continued participation in new platforms
- Manufacturing depth and operational agility - modern infrastructure, integrated processes and responsive production planning supported by automation
- Quality systems and internationally recognised certifications supporting repeat business and credibility as a long-term supplier
- Export capability and global reach through strategically located subsidiaries, notably NRF's European aftermarket distribution network and regional mega-hubs
- Bespoke engineering approach - co-creating solutions with customers using real-world usage feedback and advanced simulation tools, serving both ICE and EV platforms
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Commodity price volatility in copper, aluminium and other metals — The Company remains exposed to commodity-price movements, particularly in metals and other key inputs, which can affect margins depending on the timing and extent of cost pass-through; volatility in copper, aluminium and other metals can impact procurement costs and profitability. Mitigated through strategic sourcing, supplier development and monitoring of commodity exposures with hedging where prudent.
- Foreign exchange exposure from a heavily export- and Europe-linked business — Foreign exchange fluctuations may influence import costs and export realizations, and FX movements can impact procurement costs and profitability. The exposure is structural: exports contribute 28% of the entity's total turnover and the Company serves customers in 39 countries, with a large European footprint through NRF. Managed by monitoring FX exposures and using hedging mechanisms where prudent.
- Competitive intensity from domestic and international suppliers — The Company operates in an environment marked by competitive intensity; competition from domestic and international suppliers may affect pricing, margins and customer retention.
- Supply-chain and geopolitical disruption — Supply chains remain exposed to geopolitical developments, trade restrictions, freight volatility, natural disasters and other external disruptions. Global logistics disturbances, longer lead times and dependence on selected imported materials can create inventory and working-capital pressures. Mitigation includes diversifying vendors, developing alternate sources for critical materials, maintaining strategic inventory and strengthening supply-chain visibility. NRF's warehouse fire in France during the year demonstrated the operational-continuity exposure in practice.
- Technology transition risk - electrification and evolving product requirements — Technology change is an explicit threat: customer expectations are evolving towards lighter, more efficient and application-specific products suitable for new-generation vehicles and equipment, while the shift to electric mobility could displace conventional engine-cooling and engine-sealing demand. The Company mitigates by investing in R&D and next-generation thermal management, including through Banco New Energy Cooling Systems Limited.
- Regulatory and emission-norm change requiring continued compliance investment — Changing regulations relating to emissions, safety, environment and sustainability may require continued investments in engineering, testing and compliance (BS-VI, BS-IV/Trem V, CPCB IV+ and Stage V norms).
- Cybersecurity, data protection and IT resilience — As the Company increases its use of digital systems, cybersecurity, data protection and IT resilience remain important areas of focus. Mitigation includes next-generation firewall and endpoint detection, cyber awareness training, updated incident response and recovery protocols, and quarterly vulnerability assessment and penetration testing.
- Single-activity and product concentration — Structural concentration risk: the Company is only in one line of business - automobile components; manufacturing accounts for 100% of turnover, and radiator core and radiator assembly alone contribute 93.45% of total turnover per the BRSR product disclosure, so demand shocks in engine cooling flow directly to the whole business.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Banco engineers and manufactures heat exchangers and sealing products for demanding operating environments - radiators, charge air coolers, oil and fuel coolers, condensers, cooling modules, engine gaskets and heat shields. It serves OEMs, industrial customers and aftermarket channels across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, two- and three-wheelers, agricultural equipment, construction machinery, locomotives, gen-sets and industrial applications. The Group is progressively positioning itself as an integrated thermal-management solutions provider, supporting customers from concept and application engineering through prototype development, validation, industrialisation and series production.

business.body:
- **Engine cooling:** Radiators, Charge Air Coolers, Cooling Modules, Specialised Engine Cooling Assemblies
- **Fluid & oil cooling:** Engine Oil Coolers, Transmission Oil Coolers, Hydraulic Oil Coolers, Fuel Coolers, Application-specific Heat Exchangers
- **Next-generation thermal management:** Battery Cooling, Inverter Cooling, Power Electronics Cooling, Electric Drivetrain Thermal Management, Integrated Liquid Cooling Systems
- **Engine sealing systems:** Cylinder Head Gaskets, Engine Gaskets, Exhaust & Manifold Gaskets, Heat Shields, Industrial & Special-purpose Sealing Solutions

outlook.body:
- Technology-led growth strategy across automotive, farm and industrial equipment segments - strengthening supply relationships with existing customers through newer cooling technology models and sealing gaskets while breaking new ground with new clients in the same sectors
- Add production capabilities and bring newer performance products through R&D efforts, while adding capacities in internal fabrication and quoting facilities to improve response time and offer one-stop-shop service

- Bespoke engineering approach - co-creating customised, cost-effective and technically optimised solutions with customers using real-world usage feedback and advanced simulation tools, serving both ICE and EV platforms

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Banco Products runs 4 manufacturing plants and 4 offices in India (8 national locations; no international plants or offices of the listed entity). The Board reports that the Company continued during the year to upgrade technology and quality at its plants and has lined up an accelerated investment plan to retain its technology leadership position, with R&D capabilities including test equipment and design software being improved in line with modern practices. Management's stated operating programme is to strengthen the vendor base, expand in-house component manufacturing and invest in low-cost automation and capacity enhancement, and the MD&A outlook adds that the group continues to add production capabilities and is adding capacities in internal fabrication and quoting facilities to improve customer response time and offer one-stop-shop service. On the EV and alternative-fuel side, the Company incorporated wholly owned subsidiary Banco New Energy Cooling Systems Limited (BNCL); commercial production of heat exchangers for locomotives at BNCL's new plant in Anki, Gujarat commenced on 12th October 2023. Subsidiary Banco Gaskets (India) Limited, headquartered at Ankhi near Jambusar, operates an ISO 9001 / 16949 certified gasket plant stated to have capacity to produce over 100 million gaskets annually. European subsidiary NRF describes FY25/26 as a year of construction, securing three greenfield growth platforms on long-term leases built to NRF specifications: a new Bucharest (Romania) warehouse adding 18,613 sq m of regional warehousing, a new Florence, Italy warehouse scaling Italy from 2,000 sq m to 11,465 sq m and planned to open in June, and a new Gdansk factory that doubles factory capacity to 11,900 sq m and includes a Marine Lab and a dedicated rail refurbishment section, alongside investment in a new R&D and technical lab with advanced aftermarket equipment. NRF also expanded its range from 13,000 to 15,000 SKUs during the year with around 4,000 additional new parts in progress, and expanded OE contracts in on- and off-highway applications supported by engineering and manufacturing capacity at Banco Products (India) Limited. On the digital side the Company modernised its ERP through SAP Warehouse Management, migrated 60% of workloads to cloud/SaaS platforms, connected 30% of critical manufacturing equipment with IoT-enabled monitoring and initiated a pilot Manufacturing Execution System deployment across three plants, with a planned Zero Trust architecture, AI-based threat detection, advanced data-leakage protection, PLM implementation and SAP version upgrade still to come.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand development for the Company's products is directly dependent on developments in the user industries, where investment towards increasing production capacity and adopting new-age technologies remains the norm
- The automotive and industrial thermal-management industry is being transformed by cleaner emission norms (CPCB IV+, BS-VI, Stage V), growing demand for energy efficiency and lightweight components, and increased outsourcing by global OEMs to low-cost manufacturing countries like India
- Indian automotive industry maintained strong momentum in FY26 on robust domestic demand, infrastructure development, improving rural consumption, recovery in exports and sustained OEM investment; long-term outlook remains positive with auto-component makers positioned to benefit through innovation, localisation and OEM collaboration
- Agriculture demand supported by a favourable monsoon, higher government spending, increasing farm mechanisation, improved MSP realisation and easier access to finance, creating a positive outlook for tractors and farm equipment
- Industrial demand driven by robust GDP growth, higher public and private capital expenditure and government initiatives such as PLI, PM Gati Shakti and Make in India, with opportunity from power generation, construction, mining, railways and commercial vehicles
- India's EV market continued its strong growth trajectory in FY26 on supportive policy, domestic manufacturing investment, expanding charging infrastructure and rising consumer adoption; battery and charging improvements are expected to further accelerate EV penetration
- Global growth is scenario-driven rather than single-path: the IMF April 2026 World Economic Outlook projects global growth slowing to 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 under a limited-conflict assumption, with a base case able to shift quickly if energy prices stay elevated or trade routes are interrupted
- India's real GDP is estimated to grow 7.6% in FY 2025-26 after 7.1% in FY 2024-25 (MoSPI Second Advance Estimates, 27 February 2026); the RBI held the repo rate at 5.25% on 8 April 2026 with a neutral stance and CPI inflation was 2.75% in January 2026 and 3.4% in March 2026
- The shift away from China-centric sourcing is helping India gain mindshare with global manufacturers, though converting this into export share requires quality, reliability and delivery discipline
- Margin risk rather than volume collapse is the main concern - management's stated approach is to plan for moderate growth with sharper cost discipline rather than assume a benign macro backdrop
- Aftermarket potential from a growing vehicle population, increasing awareness of quality replacement parts and stronger service networks
- Global OEMs increasingly evaluating India as a competitive sourcing base, giving scope to convert RFQs and development enquiries into long-term business

- Banco Gaskets (India) Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned Indian subsidiary, 100% shares held; manufactures high-performance engine and industrial gaskets and sealing solutions from Ankhi near Jambusar under the BANCO brand for OEM and aftermarket customers
- Banco New Energy Cooling Systems Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned Indian subsidiary, 100% shares held; incorporated to address emerging needs in EVs and alternative fuel vehicles; commenced commercial production of heat exchangers for locomotives at its Anki, Gujarat plant on 12th October 2023
- NRF Thermal Engineering B.V. — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary of NRF Holding B.V. (100%); thermal engineering

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand development for the Company's products is directly dependent on developments in the user industries, where investment towards increasing production capacity and adopting new-age technologies remains the norm
- The automotive and industrial thermal-management industry is being transformed by cleaner emission norms (CPCB IV+, BS-VI, Stage V), growing demand for energy efficiency and lightweight components, and increased outsourcing by global OEMs to low-cost manufacturing countries like India
- Indian automotive industry maintained strong momentum in FY26 on robust domestic demand, infrastructure development, improving rural consumption, recovery in exports and sustained OEM investment; long-term outlook remains positive with auto-component makers positioned to benefit through innovation, localisation and OEM collaboration
- Agriculture demand supported by a favourable monsoon, higher government spending, increasing farm mechanisation, improved MSP realisation and easier access to finance, creating a positive outlook for tractors and farm equipment
- Industrial demand driven by robust GDP growth, higher public and private capital expenditure and government initiatives such as PLI, PM Gati Shakti and Make in India, with opportunity from power generation, construction, mining, railways and commercial vehicles
- India's EV market continued its strong growth trajectory in FY26 on supportive policy, domestic manufacturing investment, expanding charging infrastructure and rising consumer adoption; battery and charging improvements are expected to further accelerate EV penetration
- Global growth is scenario-driven rather than single-path: the IMF April 2026 World Economic Outlook projects global growth slowing to 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 under a limited-conflict assumption, with a base case able to shift quickly if energy prices stay elevated or trade routes are interrupted
- India's real GDP is estimated to grow 7.6% in FY 2025-26 after 7.1% in FY 2024-25 (MoSPI Second Advance Estimates, 27 February 2026); the RBI held the repo rate at 5.25% on 8 April 2026 with a neutral stance and CPI inflation was 2.75% in January 2026 and 3.4% in March 2026
- The shift away from China-centric sourcing is helping India gain mindshare with global manufacturers, though converting this into export share requires quality, reliability and delivery discipline
- Margin risk rather than volume collapse is the main concern - management's stated approach is to plan for moderate growth with sharper cost discipline rather than assume a benign macro backdrop
- Aftermarket potential from a growing vehicle population, increasing awareness of quality replacement parts and stronger service networks
- Global OEMs increasingly evaluating India as a competitive sourcing base, giving scope to convert RFQs and development enquiries into long-term business

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Technology-led growth strategy across automotive, farm and industrial equipment segments - strengthening supply relationships with existing customers through newer cooling technology models and sealing gaskets while breaking new ground with new clients in the same sectors
- Add production capabilities and bring newer performance products through R&D efforts, while adding capacities in internal fabrication and quoting facilities to improve response time and offer one-stop-shop service
- Strengthen the vendor base, expand in-house component manufacturing and invest in low-cost automation and capacity enhancement to improve cost competitiveness, scalability and delivery speed
- Bespoke engineering approach - co-creating customised, cost-effective and technically optimised solutions with customers using real-world usage feedback and advanced simulation tools, serving both ICE and EV platforms
- Position the Group as an integrated thermal-management solutions partner rather than a component supplier, spanning concept and application engineering, prototype development, validation, industrialisation and series production
- Deepen participation in EV and alternative-fuel applications through wholly owned subsidiary Banco New Energy Cooling Systems Limited, which commenced commercial production of heat exchangers for locomotives at its Anki, Gujarat plant
- Invest in product engineering, process improvement, automation and testing to meet BS-VI, BS-IV/Trem V and CPCB IV+ requirements, and build capability in embedded systems, application-specific solutions, digital tools and system integration
- Digital and IT roadmap - SAP Warehouse Management ERP modernisation, hybrid cloud deployment, IoT-enabled equipment monitoring, MES pilot rollout, and planned Zero Trust architecture, AI-based threat detection, advanced data-leakage protection, PLM implementation and SAP version upgrade
- NRF (European subsidiary) strategy - broaden the product range, regionalise stock availability through mega-hubs, pursue the 'Chinafication' aftermarket programme for Chinese vehicle brands starting with BYD, and build early brand leadership in EV-related aftermarket parts

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Banco Products runs 4 manufacturing plants and 4 offices in India (8 national locations; no international plants or offices of the listed entity). The Board reports that the Company continued during the year to upgrade technology and quality at its plants and has lined up an accelerated investment plan to retain its technology leadership position, with R&D capabilities including test equipment and design software being improved in line with modern practices. Management's stated operating programme is to strengthen the vendor base, expand in-house component manufacturing and invest in low-cost automation and capacity enhancement, and the MD&A outlook adds that the group continues to add production capabilities and is adding capacities in internal fabrication and quoting facilities to improve customer response time and offer one-stop-shop service. On the EV and alternative-fuel side, the Company incorporated wholly owned subsidiary Banco New Energy Cooling Systems Limited (BNCL); commercial production of heat exchangers for locomotives at BNCL's new plant in Anki, Gujarat commenced on 12th October 2023. Subsidiary Banco Gaskets (India) Limited, headquartered at Ankhi near Jambusar, operates an ISO 9001 / 16949 certified gasket plant stated to have capacity to produce over 100 million gaskets annually. European subsidiary NRF describes FY25/26 as a year of construction, securing three greenfield growth platforms on long-term leases built to NRF specifications: a new Bucharest (Romania) warehouse adding 18,613 sq m of regional warehousing, a new Florence, Italy warehouse scaling Italy from 2,000 sq m to 11,465 sq m and planned to open in June, and a new Gdansk factory that doubles factory capacity to 11,900 sq m and includes a Marine Lab and a dedicated rail refurbishment section, alongside investment in a new R&D and technical lab with advanced aftermarket equipment. NRF also expanded its range from 13,000 to 15,000 SKUs during the year with around 4,000 additional new parts in progress, and expanded OE contracts in on- and off-highway applications supported by engineering and manufacturing capacity at Banco Products (India) Limited. On the digital side the Company modernised its ERP through SAP Warehouse Management, migrated 60% of workloads to cloud/SaaS platforms, connected 30% of critical manufacturing equipment with IoT-enabled monitoring and initiated a pilot Manufacturing Execution System deployment across three plants, with a planned Zero Trust architecture, AI-based threat detection, advanced data-leakage protection, PLM implementation and SAP version upgrade still to come.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established legacy and trusted brand - more than six decades of industry experience in thermal management and sealing solutions, with a reputation for quality and reliability among OEMs, replacement-market partners and global customers
- Diversified customer, product and geographic base across automotive, agriculture, construction, industrial, power generation and aftermarket segments, reducing overdependence on any single customer, sector or geography
- Strong in-house engineering and R&D - design, testing, validation and product development capabilities enabling customised solutions aligned with changing emission norms (BS-VI, BS-IV/Trem V, CPCB IV+)
- Long-standing relationships with leading domestic and global OEMs, providing visibility into technology trends and continued participation in new platforms
- Manufacturing depth and operational agility - modern infrastructure, integrated processes and responsive production planning supported by automation
- Quality systems and internationally recognised certifications supporting repeat business and credibility as a long-term supplier
- Export capability and global reach through strategically located subsidiaries, notably NRF's European aftermarket distribution network and regional mega-hubs
- Bespoke engineering approach - co-creating solutions with customers using real-world usage feedback and advanced simulation tools, serving both ICE and EV platforms

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Commodity price volatility in copper, aluminium and other metals — The Company remains exposed to commodity-price movements, particularly in metals and other key inputs, which can affect margins depending on the timing and extent of cost pass-through; volatility in copper, aluminium and other metals can impact procurement costs and profitability. Mitigated through strategic sourcing, supplier development and monitoring of commodity exposures with hedging where prudent.
- Foreign exchange exposure from a heavily export- and Europe-linked business — Foreign exchange fluctuations may influence import costs and export realizations, and FX movements can impact procurement costs and profitability. The exposure is structural: exports contribute 28% of the entity's total turnover and the Company serves customers in 39 countries, with a large European footprint through NRF. Managed by monitoring FX exposures and using hedging mechanisms where prudent.
- Competitive intensity from domestic and international suppliers — The Company operates in an environment marked by competitive intensity; competition from domestic and international suppliers may affect pricing, margins and customer retention.
- Supply-chain and geopolitical disruption — Supply chains remain exposed to geopolitical developments, trade restrictions, freight volatility, natural disasters and other external disruptions. Global logistics disturbances, longer lead times and dependence on selected imported materials can create inventory and working-capital pressures. Mitigation includes diversifying vendors, developing alternate sources for critical materials, maintaining strategic inventory and strengthening supply-chain visibility. NRF's warehouse fire in France during the year demonstrated the operational-continuity exposure in practice.
- Technology transition risk - electrification and evolving product requirements — Technology change is an explicit threat: customer expectations are evolving towards lighter, more efficient and application-specific products suitable for new-generation vehicles and equipment, while the shift to electric mobility could displace conventional engine-cooling and engine-sealing demand. The Company mitigates by investing in R&D and next-generation thermal management, including through Banco New Energy Cooling Systems Limited.
- Regulatory and emission-norm change requiring continued compliance investment — Changing regulations relating to emissions, safety, environment and sustainability may require continued investments in engineering, testing and compliance (BS-VI, BS-IV/Trem V, CPCB IV+ and Stage V norms).
- Cybersecurity, data protection and IT resilience — As the Company increases its use of digital systems, cybersecurity, data protection and IT resilience remain important areas of focus. Mitigation includes next-generation firewall and endpoint detection, cyber awareness training, updated incident response and recovery protocols, and quarterly vulnerability assessment and penetration testing.
- Single-activity and product concentration — Structural concentration risk: the Company is only in one line of business - automobile components; manufacturing accounts for 100% of turnover, and radiator core and radiator assembly alone contribute 93.45% of total turnover per the BRSR product disclosure, so demand shocks in engine cooling flow directly to the whole business.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
